overview: This Senate resolution sets the majority party's members on four Senate committees: Appropriations (which writes federal spending bills), Armed Services, Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and Indian Affairs. It lists each senator by name, names each committee's chair, and says these assignments last for the rest of the 119th Congress or until replacements are chosen. Resolutions like this are routine housekeeping the Senate uses to fill or reshuffle committee seats. It was offered and approved by unanimous consent on March 27, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution is a routine step that keeps committees fully staffed so they can keep holding hearings and moving legislation.
against: Critics say it is purely internal housekeeping that changes no law, though committee rosters do shape which senators influence spending, defense, health and tribal policy.
